The sample includes alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls with results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend per emotion; attend emotion > attend neutral) and whole-brain second-level voxelwise analyses with standard-space coordinates and corrected thresholds. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

The full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study that uses instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: downregulate and upregulate) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (healthy participants; genotype groups reported) is acceptable, and the paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (downregulate > look, upregulate > look, negative > neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster thresholds in standard space, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met.

Although this study uses task-based fMRI (NF and backward-masking/emotional conflict tasks) and reports whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates, it does not meet the review's core requirement that participants be instructed to regulate an emotional response to visual stimuli (I6). The fMRI tasks primarily involve neurofeedback-driven downregulation of amygdala activity (NF vs rest), i.e., volitional modulation of a neural signal, rather than an instructed emotion regulation strategy applied to concurrently presented visual emotional stimuli (e.g., reappraisal of pictures). While visual stimulus tasks (backward masking; emotional conflict Stroop) are present, regulation was not instructed during those stimulus presentations. Therefore I6 is not satisfied; additionally, the within-task contrasts involving regulation do not specifically reflect instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli as required (I9 is not met for the meta-analysis target). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instruction) and thus does not meet the emotion-regulation task requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI) and I8 (sample qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I7 (regulated stimuli are written statements/sentences rather than the visual image/video stimuli specified), I9 (no within-task contrast of regulation vs. view; contrasts are illness vs. control evaluations, not regulation contrasts), and I10 (no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level task activation map surviving whole-brain correction; reported results rely on small-volume/ROI corrections). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (results are reported with small-volume corrections/ROIs rather than whole-brain-corrected findings). Therefore the study does not satisfy the review’s core inclusion requirements and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual negative pictures (I7) in a healthy sample (I8) and it reports within-task contrasts comparing inhibition-priming versus neutral-priming (I9). However, the study did not instruct participants to use any explicit emotion-regulation strategy; it used word-priming to induce automatic (implicit) regulation rather than an instructed regulation task, so it does not meet I6. Moreover, the reported neuroimaging results are presented via an ROI-focused analysis (exploratory ROI percent-signal-change and ROI-based contrasts) with no accompanying whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation tables or peak coordinates described, which fails I10 and corresponds to exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/ small-volume results with no whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) in patients with MDD and matched controls, with within-task contrasts (negative decrease > negative look) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (including Talairach coordinates and cluster-thresholded maps). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and it reports within-task effects). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to perform cognitive reappraisal (downregulate/upregulate/maintain) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts of interest (downregulate > maintain, upregulate > maintain, negative > neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses and ROI analyses, with statistical maps available on Neurovault. The sample includes younger and older adults and the analyses meet the meta-analysis requirements. Although some participants had incomplete brain coverage, whole-brain group-level results were nevertheless performed and reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion (explicit ‘decrease’ vs ‘look’ instructions), uses visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), reports within-task regulation and reactivity contrasts (decrease negative > look negative; look negative > look neutral), and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates/tables. Methods, results and discussion are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotion (diminish/enhance/maintain) using cognitive reappraisal-like strategies during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (diminish>maintain, enhance>maintain, maintain>diminish) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholding. The sample includes clinical (PTSD, trauma-exposed non-PTSD) and healthy control groups with separate reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) during an fMRI Ultimatum Game and during IAPS training, fulfilling the review focus on instructed emotion regulation. Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures in training and photographs of proposers/faces during the task). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Down > Look, Down < Look < Up, regulated decisions contrasts) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Participant sample is healthy adults and methods/results/discussion are fully presented. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or perspective-taking without regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (film clips). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > watch-negative; suppress > watch-negative; watch-negative > watch-neutral) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes a placebo regulation condition. Visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) were used. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. RU–CUR, PU–CUP and related conjunction/subtraction contrasts) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures in standard space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical paper, or empathy-only perspective tasks) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The full text meets all inclusion requirements for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; Suppress condition) during stimulus presentation (I6). Stimuli are visual (IAPS static images; I7). The sample is healthy adult participants (I8). The analyses report within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Suppress > Maintain, Maintain > Suppress) and parametric covariates of subjective ratings (I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with peak coordinates in standard space are reported (I10,I11). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation issues). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect elicited by visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The methods describe block-wise Reappraise and Maintain conditions, online self-report ratings, and within-task contrasts including conjunctions ([Maintain > Baseline] AND [Reappraise > Baseline]) used to identify amygdala activation as well as task-dependent PPI contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain). Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates (e.g., left amygdala MNI −22,0,−22) and whole-brain PPI results (Table 1, figures). The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not only ROI/only connectivity-only; whole-brain task analyses are present). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an instructed antecedent-focused emotion regulation manipulation (precedent descriptions presenting images as fictitious vs real), fulfilling the review’s definition of extrinsic/incidental reappraisal. Stimuli were visual static images (mutilation/IAPS), participants were healthy adults, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (unpleasant > neutral) and ROI paired tests showing attenuation of amygdala/insula responses. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and coordinates/peaks are reported; standard group-level analyses were used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and acceptance) during presentation of visual sad images (IAPS and normed photos). The sample includes remitted MDD and control participants with separate group analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (accept > reappraise, accept > view, reappraise > view) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported cluster results/locations in tables and text. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Although an a priori mask/SVC was noted for some analyses, whole-brain clusters outside frontal/amygdala (e.g., insula) are reported, supporting whole-brain task-evoked results. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to apply emotion-regulation strategies (mindfulness and a cognitive reappraisal “reality checking”) during the anticipation and perception of emotional pictures. Stimuli were visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., exp ng > nt, per ng > nt), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of activations, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Sample is healthy adults. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study should be excluded because the emotional stimuli being regulated are non-visual (anticipation of somatosensory pain via intraepidermal electrical stimulation), which fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). The study does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal during anticipation), I8 (eligible sample: healthy participants reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, e.g., regulation vs. anxiety), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I11 (results/coordinates described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to not meeting I7 (non-visual regulated stimuli).

This article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to perform cognitive reappraisal (interpretation/reinterpretation via contextual titles) of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (young adult university participants) is eligible. The fMRI analysis includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (IAPS2–IAPS1 for up-/down-regulation) and reports group-level whole-brain activation results with peak coordinates (e.g., left middle temporal gyrus coordinates provided; Table 2 referenced). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not review-only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without within-task effects, not an empathy task lacking regulation instructions). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), with both an at-risk clinical group and healthy controls whose results are reported separately. The analyses include within-task contrasts for regulation (Reappraisal > Attend Negative) and unregulated viewing (View Negative > View Neutral), performed as group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-task effects, not purely perspective-taking). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed an emotion regulation strategy (detachment/distancing, a form of cognitive reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS images). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation and permit conditions (e.g., Negative Detach vs. Negative Permit) and conducts second-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space; ROI analyses are supplementary. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI results, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise > look contrasts) and reports within-task contrasts. Stimuli include visual faces (fearful and neutral) used during the instruction/regulation period; although top-down generation used sentences as background, the regulated stimulus during instruction is a visual face, so the study meets the visual-stimuli requirement. The sample (healthy adult women) is acceptable. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This full-text reports a task-based BOLD fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal ("Reduce Emotion") vs maintain responses to negative images (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (I7). Participant groups include healthy controls and clinical groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Baseline; Maintain vs Baseline; and task effects/interaction) and behavioral-fMRI relationships (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented with cluster thresholds and peak coordinates in Talairach space (I10), and results are reported in tables/figures/supplement (I11). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; reports whole-brain task activation maps; not only connectivity or ROI-only; includes within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use causal attributions as an emotion-regulation strategy while viewing visual stimuli (static facial images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (internal>view, external>view, emotion-specific contrasts) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and reported coordinates/tables. Participant groups (MDD and matched healthy controls) are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging, preprocessing, statistics), Results (behavioral, fMRI, connectivity) and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, includes task activation maps, includes within-group effects, and the instructed task explicitly directs emotion regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). All relevant inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly used a cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) paradigm with instructed regulation (Suppress/reappraise) and a passive Observe condition. Emotional stimuli were visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (Maintain>Observe and Suppress>Maintain) and describes group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with correction and supplementary tables for full results/coordinates. The sample includes cocaine-dependent groups and a healthy control group with group results reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced but their absence does not render the main text incomplete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Experience; Experience > Reappraise), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain correction, and provides full methods, results, and discussion in the full text. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This article meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal: “decrease negative”) during presentation of stimuli (I6). Stimuli were visual static images (negative and neutral pictures) (I7). The sample includes clinical (female adolescents with conduct disorder) and typically developing control groups reported separately (I8). Analyses report within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (decrease negative > look negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look negative > look neutral) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted and whole-brain familywise-error-corrected results are reported (cluster-level FWE and references to peak/cluster reports), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, within-group effects are reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (static angry face photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Observe-angry, Increase > Observe-angry), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample is healthy adults and resting-state subset is reported but task analyses meet meta-analysis objectives. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise-Neg vs Maintain-Neg), uses visual stimuli (static facial images), reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation, and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activations/coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This full text reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It includes behavioral and physiological validation, within-task contrasts (e.g. Increase > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Negative), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported thresholds/coordinates. The methods, results, and discussion are complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal via distancing) in youth using visual stimuli (validated photographs), meeting the review’s core design. The paper reports within-task contrasts focused on regulation (Far) versus baseline and Far versus Look-Negative, and describes traditional univariate (GLM) whole-brain analyses with data registered to MNI152 and univariate results provided in the Supplement, satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/coordinates. The sample (typically developing children/adolescents) is eligible. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical work) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary univariate results are referenced. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative) and an unregulated viewing contrast (Attend Negative > Attend Neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and FWE cluster correction. Sample (n=62 young adults) is eligible. Although resting-state analyses are also included, the paper clearly contains task activation results, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual IAPS pictures (I7). The task explicitly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (voluntary attentional regulation: shape-evaluation vs valence-evaluation), meeting the instructed regulation criterion (I6). The sample includes MDD patients and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts tied to regulation (SRT vs ERT and valence contrasts) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM second-level tests with voxelwise and cluster-FWE thresholds and extraction of local activation peaks (I10); results/coordinates are described and supplemental tables are referenced (I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group effects are reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (Reduce vs Maintain) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reduce > Maintain and related effects), presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-correction (AlphaSim) and tables/figures of significant clusters, and includes an eligible sample (anxious and control groups). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within-task effects are reported; not an empathy/perspective task without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (cognitive reappraisal; I6) with visual stimuli (static IAPS pictures; I7). The sample includes unmedicated panic-disorder patients and healthy controls with results reported (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Reappraise; I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with standard-space coordinates and Z-values (MNI peaks cited; I10/I11). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Given the clear match to the review objective (fMRI emotion regulation to visual stimuli) and the presence of whole-brain task contrasts, the study should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) while presenting visual IAPS pictures to healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion induction and regulation (e.g., view NEG – view NEU; view NEG – distract; view NEG – reappraise) and provides peak coordinates in MNI space. The manuscript also states that complementary exploratory whole-brain analyses (Supplementary Table 1) are provided, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (coordinates reported in text/tables/supplement). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, non-empirical, connectivity-only analyses) apply.

This article meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs explicit emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and distraction (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes remitted MDD patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported (I8). Analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraisal vs. view; distraction vs. view) and viewing contrasts (I9). The paper reports group-level activation peaks in standard (MNI) space (e.g., amygdala coordinates) and thresholding information, consistent with whole-brain/voxelwise reporting (I10,I11). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs a cognitive regulation strategy (thought suppression/self-distraction) and reports whole-brain group analyses with coordinates; however it does NOT meet the meta-analysis requirement that the regulated emotional stimuli be visual. The paradigm uses anticipatory anxiety for painful electrical stimulation with auditory cues and somatosensory (pain) stimuli, so I7 (visual stimuli) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotions evoked by visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (regulate > view), performs group-level whole-brain GLM analyses with results transformed to Talairach space and provides activation coordinates (Tables/Figures). Sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (fearful/angry faces) with a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (faces > shapes). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and figures/tables, tests individual differences in reappraisal use but also provides the unregulated viewing contrast needed for the review. Although the study does not instruct emotion regulation (so it does not satisfy an instructed-regulation criterion), it meets the meta-analysis objective of including visual-stimulus viewing contrasts and provides whole-brain task activation maps appropriate for inclusion. Full text is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS and spider photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (e.g. up > look, down > look) and unregulated viewing contrasts (spider > aversive, spider > neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and text), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. Exclusion IDs met: none ([]) . Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces/objects), I8 (sample: children and adult groups allowed), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts: faces > objects and block contrasts), I10 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I11 (results described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy) — the task induced mood implicitly via point winning/losing and participants were not instructed to use any regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) or to regulate their emotional responses. Because I6 is required and not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend) of visual sad images (IAPS and other pictures) in remitted MDD and control participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise-sad > attend-sad), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported clusters/coordinates (tables/figures). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (mentalizing-reappraisal: up, down, look) during presentation of visual social stimuli (photos of proposers and monetary offers displayed on screen). The sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., DOWN > LOOK, UP > LOOK, DOWN < LOOK < UP) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates (tables/figures). Reporting meets the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and includes explicit instructions to amplify/dampen emotion). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (Detachment, Reinterpretation, Distraction, Expressive Suppression) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., ‘Regulate Negative’ > ‘Permit Negative’ and vice versa), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and presents full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adults) is eligible. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=30) that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraisal > view; distraction > view; reappraisal vs distraction), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR correction, and tables/figures with peak coordinates. Sample is healthy adults and the full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs voluntary emotion regulation (detachment/distancing) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample comprises healthy adult participants and within-task contrasts (regulated vs. non-regulated; negative vs. neutral) are reported. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (with peak coordinates and FWE correction), and amygdala ROI results are also provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment instructing emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) using visual IAPS pictures in healthy high-risk and control groups. It provides within-task contrasts (view negative > neutral; reappraisal negative > view negative; distraction positive > view positive) from second-level random-effects analyses and gives peak coordinates in MNI space for group-level contrasts. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available. Although ROI-based correction was used, group-level voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates are reported, satisfying the whole-brain coordinate reporting requirement for the meta-analysis.

This study used an implicit/incidental reappraisal manipulation (prior descriptions) but participants were not explicitly instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy. Inclusion criterion I6 requires that an emotion regulation strategy be instructed; that requirement is not met. All other relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied: task-based fMRI (I5), visual stimuli (I7), eligible sample (I8), within-task regulation-related contrast (NNEG-DESC > NEG-DESC) reported (I9), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported (I10), and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet I6 (no instructed regulation).

The article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) during presentation of visual negative and neutral pictures, satisfying I5–I7. The sample is healthy adult participants (I8). However, all activation effects are reported using ROI-based analyses (amygdala ROIs) and PPI connectivity analyses restricted to anatomically defined IFG masks. The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (analyses were mask-restricted), so it fails inclusion criterion I10 and (by implication) I11. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI / small-volume-corrected results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (food images) in an adolescent sample, and it reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > imagine eating) and whole-brain analyses. However, the provided full text does not report peak activation coordinates in a standard stereotaxic space (e.g., MNI or Talairach) or tables/figures with such coordinates, which is required by inclusion criterion I10 for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore I cannot confirm that I10 is satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met in the provided content. Based on the absence of reported peak coordinates in the supplied full text, the study must be excluded for failure to meet all required inclusion criteria.

Although this is a task-based, within-subject fMRI study reporting whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates, it fails the review's stimulus criterion. The regulated emotional stimuli are experimenter-selected negative self-belief sentences (word/sentence stimuli presented on screen). The meta-analysis exclusion explicitly excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli (I7 not met). Other inclusion criteria are satisfied (see list). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

All inclusion criteria are met: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (self-distancing/reappraisal) (I6). Regulated stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is healthy participants (female young adults), qualifying under sample criteria (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Response: Attend > Distance; Prediction Error: Distance > Attend) (I9). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with cluster-level FWE correction and reported coordinates/tables (MNI coordinate(s) and Table S2 referenced), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10) and acceptable reporting (I11). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, etc.). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with an eligible sample (I8) that reports within-task contrasts (Tenderness vs Anguish) and provides group-level whole-brain, FWE-corrected results with peak coordinates (I9, I10). However, it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements: I6 (the task does not instruct a canonical emotion-regulation strategy applied to an external stimulus such as cognitive reappraisal/acceptance/reality-checking; participants were instructed to generate/up-regulate internal emotional states via personalized recall/mantras and neurofeedback) and I7 (the regulated/emotion-eliciting stimuli were primarily non-visual: music and autobiographical imagery; the virtual environment served as neurofeedback/BCI rather than as the visual emotional stimulus to be regulated). No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E7) are directly triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 and I7 required by the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task contrasts (Regulate vs Attend). However, the paper reports ROI-based task activation analyses (extracted mean BOLD in predefined spherical ROIs) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain task activation reporting) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain task analysis). Summary: exclusion criteria met: E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal via distancing to downregulate emotion (meets I5,I6). Stimuli were visual pictures (negative, positive, neutral), meeting I7. Sample includes acute AN patients and matched healthy controls with group results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and viewing (negative watch > neutral; negative watch > negative distance; negative watch < negative distance) (I9). Group-level voxelwise analyses and whole-brain/exploratory results with peak coordinates are reported (figures/Supplementary, coordinate peaks in text), satisfying I10 and I11. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion; no exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects, not an empathy task). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate affect (up-regulate by “thinking happy thoughts” and down-regulate by “relaxing”), reports within-task regulation contrasts (up vs down), includes a suitable sample (children/adolescents), and provides group-level whole-brain analyses (see main text and supplementary Table S4/Fig S2). However, the experimental regulation was directed at internallygenerated affect via neurofeedback rather than regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli: the neurofeedback task did not present emotional visual stimuli during the regulation blocks (the visual faces were used only in the localiser), so the study does not meet the review’s requirement that the regulated stimuli be visual (I7). The meta-analysis objective specifically targets studies where participants regulate an emotional response to visual stimuli (or view them without regulating). Therefore, despite meeting several inclusion criteria, failure to meet I7 means exclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (96 IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Look) and provides peak coordinates (MNI) for activation and connectivity results, satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, imaging acquisition/analysis), Results (behavioral and fMRI), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to regulate emotion (distancing/taking the position of a noninvolved observer) versus naturally experiencing emotions while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and correction procedures (FDR whole-brain, FWE within ROIs), within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing, and detailed methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adults) is eligible. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, non-empirical, connectivity-only, or non-regulation perspective-taking without emotion regulation) are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore this study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (increase/decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (static face photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation to view ([increase + decrease] > view) and describes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and identified peak regions (reported in tables). The sample includes both patients with lifetime MDD and matched healthy controls with results reported across/within groups. These features satisfy all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5–I11). The full text provided contains methods, results, and tables/figures described, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) during presentation of visual emotional images (IAPS and Internet pictures). The sample (healthy adult women) is acceptable. The paper reports within-task contrasts of regulation conditions (e.g., REAP vs ESUP, NAT vs REAP), behavioral and fMRI results, and second-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full article reports an fMRI task with instructed cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during anticipation of visual reward cues (coins). Methods and analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (regulate > permit and interactions), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and appropriate correction, and task-based design. Sample is healthy adults. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply; full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, instructed up-/down-regulation). Although the study is a task-based fMRI experiment with visual stimuli (video game) and reports within-task contrasts comparing violent versus non-violent events, it measured natural/emergent emotion regulation rather than instructed regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — video gameplay), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., violent action > non-violent action), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps reported), I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed affect-labeling task (affect label vs gender label), an incidental emotion regulation strategy applied to visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts and pre/post treatment paired analyses, whole-brain PPI and activation results with peak MNI coordinates and cluster-level correction, and separates reports for SAD and healthy control groups. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete.

This study must be excluded. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the study reports only resting-state/ALFF analyses tied to pre/post cognitive tasks and does not report any whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for an emotion-regulation task. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I8 — sample criteria satisfied (older adults, clinical MCI and healthy controls reported separately). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — not a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (the fMRI was resting-state before/after tasks, not task-evoked fMRI); I6 — no instructed emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/other regulation instructions); I7 — emotional stimuli were not visual emotional images or films (affective response was to cognitive tasks, not visual emotional stimuli); I9 — no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation with visual emotional stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain peak coordinates, but it does NOT instruct participants to use an explicit emotion-regulation strategy. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups reported separately), I9 (reports within-task/unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (uses whole-brain contrasts with peak coordinates to define seeds), I11 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; the experiment manipulated pain but did not ask participants to reappraise, accept, or otherwise intentionally regulate their emotions). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (explicit instruction to regulate), which is required by the review’s inclusion criteria.

This is a randomized, placebo-controlled, task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (distraction vs. passive viewing) using visual IAPS pictures, reports within-task contrasts (distract-negative > attend-negative; attend-negative > attend-neutral), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates and statistical maps. Both PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply: the paper is empirical, reports whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), includes within-task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instruction. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that explicitly instructed participants to regulate negative emotions (increase/decrease) after errors and reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain coordinates; however, it does not examine regulation of emotional responses to visual affective stimuli (I7). The emotion that is regulated is internally generated by error commission during a cognitive task rather than being evoked by visual emotional images/films/facial expressions. Therefore it does not match the meta-analysis requirement that the regulated stimuli be visual emotional stimuli. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the full text. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, view) while viewing visual threat-related images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (increase>view, decrease>view), trial-by-trial correlations, and group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present. Sample (healthy adult females) is eligible. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not connectivity-only, not ROI-only reporting).

This study is excluded because it does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (inclusion criterion I6 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual stimuli (faces) (I7), includes an eligible sample (I8), reports within-task emotional contrasts/unregulated viewing effects (I9), and describes group-level whole-brain analyses in standard (Talairach) space with supplementary results (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Specifically: Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy or regulation contrast such as reappraise>look). Full text judged complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an emotion label vs match task (implicit emotion regulation). Participants were instructed to label emotions (an instructed task that engages implicit emotion regulation), using visual stimuli (facial expressions). The paper reports within-task contrasts (emotion label > emotion match), whole-brain group-level analyses with cluster thresholds and MNI peak coordinates, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (early-adolescent participants) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is task-based fMRI with visual stimuli and a suitable sample, and it reports trial-level task effects and relationships with behavior. However, it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraise/down-regulate instructions); instead it measures spontaneous expression of an emotion-regulation pattern, so inclusion criterion I6 (instructed regulation) is not met. Additionally, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map with peak coordinates; analyses are ROI-based and pattern-expression based without reported whole-brain activation coordinates, violating exclusion criterion E4. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (“realize being safe”) during presentation of visual social images (IAPS and additional erotic images). The paper reports within-task contrasts of regulation (negative-safe versus negative-look) and unregulated viewing (negative-look versus neutral-look), and conducts group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported cluster coordinates. Participants include clinical (BPD and cluster-C) and nonpatient control groups reported separately. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an instructed emotion-regulation (reappraisal) task using visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing high-control (reappraise) vs low-control (rate) and presents whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with peak coordinates (tables and figures). Sample qualifies (healthy adults). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual facial stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts, but it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy during scanning (I6 not met). The paper uses an ROI-focused analysis (family-wise error within predefined ROIs) and presents ROI-derived coordinates rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map, so it lacks qualifying whole-brain results (I10 not met) and thus meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study cannot be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotion (explicit ‘regulate’ vs ‘view’ cues), using visual stimuli (IAPS and photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulate negative > view negative; regulate positive > view positive), group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported MNI peak coordinates and thresholds, and also provides results in the text/tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly addresses the review objective: participants received instructed emotion-regulation strategies (goal intentions vs implementation intentions) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulate > attend, attend > regulate), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial, reported activations, coordinate conversions), ROI and connectivity analyses, and behavioral and physiological measures. Sample is healthy adults and the full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria listed below.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotion elicited by visual stimuli (spider photographs). It reports within-task contrasts (regulate vs watch) and both ROI and whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses (with supplementary tables/figures), and follows participants (including clinical spider-phobic sample) with behavioral outcomes. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (Reappraise > Maintain in the ERT) and includes unregulated viewing contrasts (Maintain > baseline, Fearful > Happy). Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures and emotional faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts and describes voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analysis with cluster correction and reports peak coordinates for DLPFC (x,y,z = −40,12,28), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) in which participants were explicitly instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy (“reality checking”) to down-regulate responses during presentation of negative emotional faces (I6). Stimuli are visual (static emotional faces) (I7). Sample is healthy adults with results reported at group level (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (contrast “view > regulate” and beta estimates used in repeated-measures ANOVA) (I9). Analyses include whole-brain GLM and report Talairach coordinates/peak locations in tables (I10) and these whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text is complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Overall, the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs an explicit emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and compares it with a placebo and passive viewing. Emotional stimuli are visual (disgust images/IAPS), the sample is healthy adults (female), and the paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g. Reappraisal (Disgust>Neutral), Passive Viewing (Disgust>Neutral)) and whole-brain group-level analyses (voxelwise SPM results with FWE correction). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual IAPS stimuli and whole-brain group analyses reporting unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., expectation/presentation negative > neutral). However, the study does not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, or other instructed regulation during anticipation or stimulus). They only assessed habitual regulation via ERQ post-scan. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met, so the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly investigates instructed emotion regulation (‘Enhance’ vs ‘Watch’) using visual stimuli (positive and neutral images from EmoPicS). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. PosUp > PosWatch, Up > Watch) and both ROI and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Sample and procedures are detailed and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to up-regulate and down-regulate emotional responses during viewing of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (‘increase’ vs ‘attend’ for positive pictures; ‘decrease’ vs ‘attend’ for negative pictures) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected, coordinates reported in tables/figures) as well as ROI analyses. The sample is adult and reported group-level task activation maps. The methods, results and discussion are present in full. All predefined inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Full-text reports a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Look conditions) with visual IAPS images, single-trial/block contrasts (Look-Negative>Look-Neutral; Reappraise>Look-Neutral), and a whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis reporting MNI peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results. The sample includes a clinical GAD group and healthy controls with results reported separately. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore complete. Meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease > attend for negative images), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and cluster-thresholding, and presents results in tables/figures. Sample includes both depressed patients and matched controls with separate group analyses. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (Reappraise vs Maintain) using visual stimuli (IAPS negative scenes; faces). The sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise>Maintain) and other within-task contrasts (Surprise>Neutral, Fear>Neutral), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and peak coordinates (ROI coordinates and cluster results described). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (positive and minimizing reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample is healthy adults, analyses include within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > natural), and the paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (reappraise and distract) while participants view sad images (visual stimuli). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Sad-Reappraise > Sad-View, Sad-Distract > Sad-View) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects analyses in MNI space with tables/figures of cluster results. The sample and analyses meet eligibility and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-only, not empathy-without-regulation). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a visual faces task (faces > shapes) that evokes affective processing. It reports within-task contrasts (faces > shapes) at the group level, with second-level voxelwise analyses in SPM5 and figures/tables (MNI reference) indicating whole-brain task-evoked results. The sample includes clinical (late-life depressed) and control groups reported separately. Analyses are not restricted to ROI-only or connectivity-only approaches. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual-task or unregulated viewing fMRI studies and provides whole-brain coordinates/activation maps suitable for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli in an adolescent sample and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts (appetitive > aversive) with peak coordinates. However, participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); rather, they performed an inhibitory go/no-go task while emotional images were presented as incidental distractors. Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy). All other relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11), and no exclusion criteria from the list apply. Because I6 is not met, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive self-distancing/reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The methods describe standard SPM8 whole-brain preprocessing and GLM contrasts (e.g., US-Paired: CER>NoCER) used to define PFC seeds and report ROI coordinates (ventral striatum center x=26,y=6,z=-8), and the Results present within-task regulation contrasts and connectivity effects. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply (no non-empirical article, not limited to only ROI/connectivity without whole-brain task maps, and within-task contrasts are reported). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study instructing participants to down-regulate their emotional response to visual (aversive) pictures, and it reports within-task contrasts (e.g. 'regulate>view'). However, the reported task results are presented primarily using region-of-interest analyses and small-volume corrections (amygdala and a vmPFC ROI). The paper does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space that would qualify as a whole-brain task result. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI/SVC results with no accompanying whole-brain task analysis).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotional responses using interpersonal cognitive reappraisal (disengage, view, engage) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS and photographs). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts (disengage>view, engage>view, linear contrasts) and unregulated viewing contrasts (negative>neutral), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates, and includes full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Sample (24 healthy women) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and includes instructed regulation). Full text appears complete. Based on these points the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The article reports an original task-based fMRI experiment using an instructed emotion-regulation task (explicit reappraisal ‘regulate’ vs ‘watch’), with visual emotional stimuli (30s film/video clips). The sample spans ages 23–88 (population-derived cohort). Analyses include within-task contrasts (e.g., negative regulate > negative watch; positive watch > neutral) and both ROI and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (whole-brain results thresholded at p<0.05 FWE), with reported task-evoked activations. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (only ROI results, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

Summary: This is a task-based fMRI study of mindfulness/MBCT in bipolar patients that instructs an acceptance/open-awareness strategy and reports within-task contrasts (meditate > control) and whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation-like strategy: acceptance/open awareness), I8 (clinical sample with control group), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to the instructed regulation task), I10 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 — the emotional stimuli are not visual; the task involved internal mindfulness/meditation without presentation of visual emotional images or film clips, whereas the meta-analysis requires regulation or viewing of visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to regulate emotion (increase vs. attend vs. decrease) using cognitive reappraisal-style strategies while viewing visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (increase>attend, decrease>attend) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected clusters and coordinates (tables/figures). Sample characteristics are acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (“reality checking”) during the anticipation (cue) period, using visual IAPS pictures as stimuli in healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and emotion (e.g. negative vs neutral; comparisons of cognitive-control vs basic groups), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with Talairach coordinates and statistical thresholds. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (subjects cued to reduce positive or negative emotion), using visual stimuli (IAPS and images), and reporting within-subject contrasts (regulate vs view). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed with peak coordinates in MNI space and conjunction/contrast results described. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly tests instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal-style “suppress” and “enhance” instructions) while participants view visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (negative suppress vs. attend; positive enhance vs. attend) and performs voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses normalized to MNI space with reported peak coordinates and cluster correction. The sample (patients with MDD) is an eligible participant group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes within-task contrasts, not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (images of high-fat/high-sugar foods; I7) with an eligible sample (young adults; I8). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., high-fat/sugar food > vegetables, high-fat/sugar food > water) and group analyses (I9). The authors explicitly state they used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholding (I10) and report results in the text/tables (I11). However, the fMRI tasks did NOT instruct participants to apply an emotion-regulation strategy during scanning: participants were asked to attend to pictures and were explicitly NOT asked to apply cognitive reappraisals (no instructed reappraisal condition), so inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet the mandatory I6 requirement.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (volitional emotion regulation) using visual IAPS pictures. It reports within-task contrasts comparing Reappraise versus Maintain and includes whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation analyses (activation results and tables of coordinates) and supplementary tables/figures. All relevant inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary materials).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal or other instructed cognitive regulation); participants were instructed simply to view images while a bitter aftertaste was present. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (fMRI task with an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is NOT met. Exclusion criteria: none of E3–E7 apply (whole-brain task activation reported; not a review; not connectivity-only; within-task effects reported; not an empathy/perspective-taking-only study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion applied because I6 not satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (reinterpretation) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Negative; Negative > Reappraise), behavioral indices of reappraisal success, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and FDR correction. An ROI analysis on amygdala is also reported, but whole-brain results are present. Sample (undergraduate high vs low psychosis proneness) is acceptable. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotional faces in pediatric bipolar disorder and therefore meets several inclusion items (I5: task-based fMRI; I7: visual stimuli—faces; I8: eligible sample with patient and control groups; I9: within-task valence comparisons/contrasts (angry vs neutral); I11: results include tables of coordinates). However it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy—participants performed a two-back working memory task with no reappraisal or other regulation instructions) and I10 (the paper does not report a conventional group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map/contrast; the reported peak coordinates derive from ICA functional-connectivity spatial maps rather than standard task activation contrasts). This study therefore falls under exclusion criterion E5 (reports connectivity-only analyses without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps). Because at least one exclusion criterion is met and important inclusion criteria are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s stimulus and whole-brain reporting requirements. It is a task-based fMRI study with instructed self-regulation (rtfMRI neurofeedback using autobiographical recall) and reports within-task contrasts and ROI/effective-connectivity results; however, the regulated stimuli are internally generated autobiographical memories rather than externally presented visual emotional stimuli (violating I7). The paper focuses on ROI-based and effective-connectivity (VAR/SVAR) analyses and does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map with peak coordinates (violating I10) and thus falls under exclusions for reporting only ROI/seed-based connectivity/effective-connectivity results (E5) and ROI-only/partial-coverage results (E4). Therefore it fails required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria.

Full-text report describes an event-related, task-based fMRI study using the SEAT paradigm with instructed emotion modulation (appraisal 'Like/Dislike' and attentional modulation conditions). Stimuli are visual (faces and scenes). The paper reports within-task condition effects (implicit emotion processing vs baseline and condition-specific simple effects), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE correction. The report includes methods, results, and discussion (full article content present). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects).

This is a task-based fMRI study (Go/NoGo) using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (aversive > neutral) as a whole-brain, voxelwise group analysis with reported peak coordinates. The task is not an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (no reappraisal instruction), but the meta-analysis objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for unregulated visual emotional stimulus viewing analyses (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11) and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

All inclusion criteria are met: this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; I6). Stimuli are visual negative IAPS images (I7). The sample is a clinical group (panic disorder) which is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g. Reappraisal > Maintain, Maintain > Reappraisal, images > baseline) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with thresholding and reported MNI coordinates (I10), and results are clearly described in the text with coordinate details (I11).
