No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain analyses, not only connectivity, includes within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study employed resting-state fMRI connectivity during anticipation of a public speech and did not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses to visual stimuli. Inclusion met: I8 (sample: clinical group with separate control group reported). Inclusion NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli; task-free/resting-state), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only seed-based/resting-state connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This study does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses; instead it manipulates financial incentive context (fixed wage vs performance-based) which may implicitly change emotion-related processing but does not meet the review’s requirement for an instructed regulation task. Exclusion criteria met: E7 (perspective-taking/self-or other-oriented task with no instruction to amplify or dampen emotion) applies because participants assumed a role and no regulation instruction was given. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—photos of faces), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts such as emotion > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no explicit instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal or similar). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study with bereaved and control groups and reports whole-brain Grief > Neutral contrasts with MNI peak coordinates, it does not meet critical inclusion criteria for this review. The ecStroop task used idiographic word stimuli (grief-related words), and the review excludes studies whose stimuli are word/sentence-based rather than visual images or video (I7 not met). Additionally, participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instruction), so I6 (instructed regulation) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal/distancing to suppress sadness (methods: explicit reappraisal training and instructions). Emotional stimuli are visual film clips (qualifies per I7). Sample: healthy children (girls aged 8–10) — eligible per I8. Analyses include within-task contrasts and an interaction contrast isolating regulation effects (e.g., Sadness/Reappraisal vs Sadness/No Reappraisal), and report group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (SPM99), with tables of loci—meeting I9–I11. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no-only-ROI, connectivity-only, or non-empirical issues). Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment (patients with generalized SAD) that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (‘Reframe’ vs ‘Just Watch’) while participants viewed dynamic visual social evaluation video clips. Emotional stimuli are visual (video clips). The authors report within-task contrasts (react and reappraise trials versus asterisk baseline; reappraise vs react examined in connectivity) and test pre-to-post treatment changes. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level random-effects maps with Talairach-space results and cluster-correction; peak coordinates and cluster statistics are reported. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not a non-empirical paper, and task includes instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) and reports whole-brain task activation and emotion contrasts, but it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy. The affective Stroop requires counting numerosity while emotional images act as distractors; participants were not instructed to reappraise, accept, distance, or otherwise regulate their emotional responses. Thus, inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task emotion contrasts/unregulated viewing), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual face stimuli that reports within-task contrasts (emotional face vs no-face) with peak coordinates and separate participant groups, so it meets I5, I7, I8, I9 and I11. However participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/etc. instructions)—the task required WM performance while ignoring emotional distracters—so I6 is not met. Analyses are restricted to ROI-based group tests (WFU PickAtlas masks and AlphaSim within ROIs) with no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, so I10 is not met. Because the paper reports only ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis, exclusion criterion E4 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based, empirical fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation (‘decrease’ vs ‘attend’) using cognitive reappraisal-like instructions, with visual stimuli (photographs and IAPS images). The sample (n=16 after exclusions) is a healthy adult group. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g. decrease > attend, stigma > IAPS) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and involves instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study with explicit instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal REAP and suppression ESUP) and a natural viewing condition. Emotional stimuli are visual static images (IAPS and photos) with social/nonsocial categories. Sample includes 19 healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., social pleasant vs nonsocial pleasant; effects during NAT, REAP, ESUP) and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and SPM maps. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive emotion regulation (detachment/distancing) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and other pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., permit > regulate, pF > rF) and group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and MNI coordinates (amygdala maxima and other whole-brain activations described), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Sample is healthy adult females and behavioral/neural results are reported. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not only ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study that presents visual emotional stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task contrasts comparing negative vs neutral clips (unregulated viewing). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with reported clusters/peaks (tables/figures) and supplementary material. Although participants were not instructed to use an explicit regulation strategy (I6 not met), the review’s inclusion allows unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), which this study provides. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain analyses (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraise/down-regulate/up-regulate/acceptance instruction); participants performed an emotion-identification/ignore-word interference task rather than an instructed regulation task. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text is complete.

Full text is complete. Meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual static image stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), and I11 (coordinates and results clearly described). Does NOT meet I6: participants were instructed simply to view/fixate the pictures (no instructed emotion regulation strategy such as reappraisal, distancing, or acceptance). Consequently it also fails I9: there is no within-task contrast explicitly indexing an instructed emotion-regulation condition (e.g., “reappraise > look”); reported contrasts compare contextual image conditions (religious vs non-religious) but do not reflect an instructed regulation manipulation. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study should be excluded for failing required inclusion criteria I6 and I9.

Full text shows a task-based fMRI study that instructed emotion-regulation strategies (feel, accept, analyze) and reports whole-brain group analyses and within-task regulation contrasts. However, the emotional stimuli are autobiographical memories cued by words/phrases (script-driven imagery), not visual stimuli (no pictures, faces, scenes, or film). Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI task study of pain controllability but does not meet key eligibility requirements for this review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I11 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; participants were allowed to stop pain but were not instructed to perform cognitive reappraisal or another directed regulation strategy), I7 (regulated stimuli are somatosensory electrical pain, not VISUAL stimuli), I9 (the within-task contrasts pertain to controllability/analgesia rather than an instructed emotion-regulation vs view contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it does not involve instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (IAPS) with healthy adult participants; it reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts for valence and arousal and presents group-level whole-brain statistical maps. However, the task involved incidental emotion rating and did not instruct any emotion regulation strategy nor report any emotion-regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look), so it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 (instruction to regulate).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal by distancing) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS interpersonal images). Behavioral and imaging results report within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. distance > look; look > distance; negative > neutral) and interaction contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster tables in standard (MNI) space; small-volume correction was used only for the amygdala in addition to whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal (Regulate) strategy versus a control (Attend) during a sequential investment task. The stimuli are visual market displays presented on-screen and evoke emotional/regret responses related to financial decisions. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Regulate and Attend and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates (MNI) and thresholding, plus tables in Supporting Information. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain, within-task contrasts, but it does NOT meet the required inclusion criterion I6: an instructed emotion-regulation strategy. The study examines implicit/spontaneous derogation (participants were not instructed to reappraise or otherwise regulate their emotions) and contrasts (reject>accept) reflect inferred, not instructed, regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation/unregulated viewing), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I6 (no instructed regulation). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails I6.

This full text reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study in children with visual emotional stimuli and within-task contrasts (fearful faces during Winning vs Recovery). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces/objects), I8 (sample: children included), I9 (reports within-task contrast related to emotional context: Winning > Recovery for fearful-face events), and I10 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported). However, it fails the key inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no instructed reappraisal or other explicit regulation instruction); the authors explicitly note there was no condition with explicit regulation instruction. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6) and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (explicit emotion regulation) while participants view visual stimuli (negative images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraisal vs. Maintain and Reappraisal vs. Fixation), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-correction thresholds, and includes ROI analyses for the amygdala. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (explicit ‘reality checking’/reappraisal) during anticipation and perception of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (exp negative > neutral; perc negative > neutral) and group comparisons, provides whole-brain, group-level analyses with cluster correction and refers to coordinate tables/supplementary material. The sample (patients with SAD, with cognitive-control and basic groups) is eligible, and the full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, within-group effects reported, and not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI emotion regulation with visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study in adolescent girls that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (‘‘decrease’’/distancing) during an emotion regulation paradigm using visual stimuli (IAPS and youth images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., decrease > look; look negative > look neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak activations and cluster correction in standard space. The full text includes introduction, methods (tasks, acquisition, preprocessing, ROI/PPI), results (behavioral, whole-brain, ROI, connectivity), and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet two required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis: I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) and I7 (emotional stimuli are visual images/film). Instead, the fMRI tasks directed participants to engage in rumination (provocation-focused, self-focused, neutral-focused), which is not an instructed regulation strategy such as reappraisal/acceptance, and the emotional stimuli/feedback and prompts were presented as written text (word/sentence stimuli). The study does meet several other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample with group results), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as feedback > pre-feedback baseline and provocation-focus > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (coordinates/whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for failure to satisfy I6 and I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=24) that instructed participants to regulate emotion using cognitive reappraisal (decrease) versus view, with visual IAPS pictures as stimuli. The paper reports within-task contrasts (decrease–view) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FWE cluster-corrected results, figures and tables of coordinates, as well as ROI analyses. Participant sample details and full methods, results and discussion are provided in the full text. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

Excluded because the fMRI task did not involve an instructed emotion regulation strategy (inclusion criterion I6 not met). The study used a face–word emotional conflict task that measures implicit emotion conflict adaptation rather than an instructed regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (eligible sample: older adults), I9 (reports within-task contrast related to emotion regulation: iI vs cI), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 applicable). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

The study is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I7: the emotional stimuli regulated are internally-generated autobiographical memories (imagery), not visual stimuli (e.g., pictures, films, faces). It does meet several other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task to upregulate positive emotion via autobiographical recall), I8 (healthy adult sample reported), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as train>rest and happy>rest), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates), and I11 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the meta-analysis requires regulated stimuli to be visual and this study uses non-visual, internally-driven stimuli, it does not satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal to increase and decrease negative affect) using visual stimuli (IAPS photographs). The sample (healthy female participants) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (increase > look, decrease > look, look > decrease) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Full text is complete and includes methods, results, and discussion. Accordingly, it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not meet key stimulus and task requirements for this meta-analysis. The emotional stimuli were auditory/script-driven stories (non-visual), violating inclusion I7 (visual stimuli required). Participants were instructed to take the protagonist’s perspective during listening (perspective-taking) with no instruction to amplify or dampen their own emotional response, which matches exclusion E7 (perspective-taking studies without regulation). The study does meet several other criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I8: eligible sample including controls; I9: reports within-task emotion contrasts, e.g., anger > neutral; I10: group-level whole-brain analyses reported; I11: results presented in text/figures). However, it does not satisfy I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy) and I7 (stimuli non-visual). Given these violations, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use two emotion-regulation strategies (Observe — a mindfulness/acceptance instruction — and Suppress) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Suppress-negative vs. Look-negative; Observe-negative vs. Look-negative; Look-negative vs. Look-neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholding described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review (task-based fMRI, instructed regulation, visual stimuli, any sample, within-task contrasts, whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: an instructed emotion-regulation/self-focused strategy—emotion-introspection—was used; I8: clinical sample reported; I9: within-task contrasts related to the instructed strategy were reported (e.g. ‘feel’>‘think’, ‘feel’>‘neutral’); I10/I11: group-level whole-brain analyses and coordinates/thresholding are reported). However it fails the stimulus requirement (I7): the regulated emotional content was internally generated (participants introspected on their current emotions) rather than regulation of visually presented emotional stimuli. The only visual material were neutral IAPS distractor images presented after trials, not emotional visual stimuli to be regulated. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore I exclude the study because it does not satisfy I7 (visual emotional stimuli).

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses rather than a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Exclusion criteria met: E4. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-control strategy: participants were instructed to ignore emotional distractors/engage voluntary attentional control), I7 (visual stimuli: emotional faces), I8 (sample includes patients and matched healthy controls reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotion presence/regulation: emotional-face vs no-face contrasts during 2-back). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps with peak coordinates reported; analyses were ROI-based). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for failing I10 and meeting exclusion E4.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study with an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (CBT-like reappraisal/reality-checking strategies), uses visual stimuli (IAPS images), reports results separately for MDD patients and matched controls, includes within-task contrasts (reduce vs attend, enhance vs attend), and presents whole-brain group-level analyses with reported cluster coordinates and tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (supplementary data noted but not required). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (static facial photographs) and an implicit emotion-processing task (gender discrimination). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (angry>scrambled, fearful>scrambled, sad>scrambled, happy>scrambled, neutral>scrambled) and conducts group-level whole-brain analyses with reported clusters. Participant groups (MDD, Anx, DAC, HC) are reported separately. Although no emotion-regulation instructions were used, the review objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; thus the study meets the meta-analysis scope. Full text contains introduction, methods, analyses, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply.

Full text reviewed. Exclusion: none of the explicit exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample: healthy adults), I9 (reports within-task, unregulated viewing contrasts: self-critical > neutral, etc.), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; participants were told to read words and attend to feelings, but were not instructed to reappraise or otherwise regulate), I7 (regulated/viewed stimuli are words/adjectives presented visually; the review excludes studies whose stimuli are word and sentence stimuli). Because two core inclusion criteria (I6 and I7) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis despite being a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain results.

Full text presents a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise>Maintain) at the group level and gives peak coordinates in MNI space. Both a clinical PTSD group and a combat-exposed control group are included and analyzed. Although primary inference used an ROI mask with cluster correction, the authors also conducted whole-brain analyses (reported as yielding no additional significant clusters), and group-level voxelwise maps with standard-space peaks are provided. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E4 applies: the study reports primarily ROI/mask-based voxelwise analyses (a priori ROIs: left/right amygdala and insula; exploratory larger ROI mask) and does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map in standard space. Consequently inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. The study does satisfy: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed implicit emotion-regulation paradigm via attend/ignore instructions qualifies as instructed cognitive control), I7 (visual stimuli—faces and houses), I8 (sample reported; clinical group with controls), and I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation/attention: attend vs ignore fearful faces and emotion×attention interactions). Because I10 is not met and E4 is triggered (ONLY ROI/mask results), the study is excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (detach/experience) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Positive-Experience > Positive-Regulate; Negative-Regulate > Negative-Experience), trial-by-trial parametric analyses, and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with MNI coordinates and cluster correction (tables/figures). Sample includes younger and older adults. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, sufficient for screening. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based/small-volume-corrected task activation results with no accompanying whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level activation maps, violating exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adults), and I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts such as anticipation > baseline and condition contrasts). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — participants performed an anticipation/viewing task without regulation instructions) and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical maps reported), and therefore I11 (reporting of whole-brain results) is also not applicable. Full text appears complete. Because E4 is met (ONLY ROI/SVC results reported), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting several other inclusion items.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and suppression) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (video clips). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise/suppress > watch), presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (Talairach), and includes full methods, results, and discussion. The sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs participants to regulate negative emotion (reappraisal/distancing, suppression, distraction) while viewing visual IAPS pictures, and also includes unregulated viewing. It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulated vs. unregulated aversive stimulation (e.g., Stim_RegAv > Stim_Av and Stim_Av > Stim_RegAv), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM GLM; whole-brain FWE-corrected results and reported peak coordinates/figures/tables). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core details (participants, task, imaging, preprocessing, statistics, contrasts, coordinates) are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (emotional faces > shapes) as well as whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates (amygdala xyz reported; supplementary material referenced). Participant sample (SAD patients) is acceptable. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given, the review objective includes studies that simply view emotional stimuli without regulating, and the paper reports the necessary within-task contrasts. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for unregulated viewing contrasts and provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which children passively viewed visual emotional stimuli (faces) and task-evoked activations were reported. The study reports unregulated viewing contrasts (face conditions vs. fixation/baseline and emotion effects), whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and reported regional effects, and peak/cluster results consistent with standard reporting. The sample (4–6-year-old clinical and control groups) is eligible. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (no reappraisal/down-regulation task), the review protocol accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), so the study fits the meta-analysis objective of including viewing-only studies. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the report appears complete.

This is an fMRI neurofeedback task with instructed regulation (recall of positive autobiographical memories) in a clinical sample and whole-brain voxelwise analyses, but the regulated emotional stimuli are internally-generated memories rather than external VISUAL stimuli (no IAPS/images/film clips). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (within-task task activation contrasts/ regressors for neurofeedback/happy blocks), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I11 (maps/tables/figures described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (fear and neutral faces; I7) in an eligible sample (adults; I8). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (fear > neutral anticipation) and within-group effects (I9). The authors also performed and reported an exploratory whole-brain voxel-wise analysis with cluster thresholds and coordinates (I10, I11). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not applicable for unregulated-viewing studies), the meta-analysis objective permits inclusion of unregulated viewing studies. Full text is complete and contains methods, results, and coordinates for whole-brain analyses. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for inclusion as an unregulated viewing task-based fMRI study of visual emotional stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Maintain vs Reappraisal) using visual IAPS images, reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Reappraise), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. The sample (patients with panic disorder, randomized to treatment vs waiting) is acceptable per inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (study does not report only ROI/SVC or only connectivity; whole-brain analyses are present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study should be excluded because the emotional stimuli regulated were written, personally-relevant worry statements (word/sentence stimuli presented on screen). Inclusion criterion I7 requires visual emotional stimuli such as images or film/video; the review explicitly excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word and sentence stimuli. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation including acceptance), I8 (sample qualifies—clinical GAD sample reported), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., Accept > Worry, Suppress > Accept), I10 (group-level second-level random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates), and I11 (coordinates/whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered based on the full text provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because inclusion criterion I7 is not met (regulated stimuli were word/sentence-based rather than visual images/videos).

This is a task-based fMRI study that used an emotion regulation paradigm (participants were cued to “look” or to reappraise), with visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (look negative > look neutral) and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI). Sample and analyses meet eligibility (adolescents; clinical and control data reported). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study must be excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met): participants performed a color-naming/ignore-the-word task rather than being instructed to reappraise, accept, distance, or otherwise regulate their emotional response. Stimuli are word stimuli (visual words), which are explicitly excluded by the review criterion (I7 not met: the review requires visual images/films; word/sentence stimuli are excluded). The study also does not report a within-task contrast of instructed emotion regulation vs viewing (I9 not met): reported contrasts are unpleasant vs neutral (emotional interference) and connectivity analyses, not regulate>view or similar. It does satisfy I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps with standard-space coordinates) and I11 (coordinates/tables reported). Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in an eligible sample and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (NEG–NEU) with peak coordinates, it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. The fMRI task presented words (visual word stimuli) rather than images or videos, and the manuscript does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/regulated > unregulated contrast). Thus it fails I6 (no instructed emotion regulation) and I7 (stimuli are words, which the protocol excludes). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal of appetitive visual stimuli (personally craved food images) and compares regulated and unregulated viewing. The task is a within-subjects fMRI craving-regulation paradigm (look vs regulate) with a choice manipulation; behavioral and neural contrasts (e.g., regulate > look, look > regulate, yes > no) are reported. Analyses include second-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects models using SPM/DARTEL with cluster correction and reported MNI peak coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task contrasts, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only design). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that includes an instructed emotion-regulation condition: affect labeling (participants verbally label facial emotions), which functions as an incidental/instructed regulation strategy (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual (static face images) (I7). The sample includes patient (methamphetamine-dependent) and control groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (affect label vs affect match; and emotion viewing contrasts) (I9). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and tables of clusters/coordinates are provided (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity), includes within-group effects, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This task-based fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I5: It is a task-based fMRI experiment. I6: The protocol included an instructed regulation condition (“Reframe”), indicating an emotion-regulation strategy was part of the task battery. I7: Emotional stimuli were visual (looming faces, dynamic video clips, and visually-presented autobiographical sentences/negative self-beliefs); videos and written sentences are acceptable visual stimuli. I8: Participant sample is acceptable (clinical SAD group and healthy controls reported separately). I9: The paper reports within-task contrasts related to unregulated viewing (React versus Asterisks) for each task. I10: Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported with cluster coordinates and tables. I11: Whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI results, only connectivity, or only between-group effects without within-task effects. Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) during presentation of visual IAPS photographs, reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. decrease > attend, increase > attend), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Talairach peak coordinates and corrected clusters. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met) with an eligible sample (I8 met). It reports within-task emotion contrasts (unpleasant > neutral; pleasant > neutral) so unregulated viewing contrasts are available (I9 met) and it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with tabulated results (I10 and I11 met). However, the study does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met) and the emotional stimuli are words (emotion-word Stroop), which the protocol excludes (I7 not met: the review excludes studies whose stimuli are word/sentence-based rather than visual images/films). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (specifically I6 and I7), the study is excluded.

This is an empathy-focused task fMRI study without any instructed emotion regulation (no reappraisal/distancing/other regulation instructions). Although it reports task-evoked whole-brain visual stimulus activations, it does not instruct participants to amplify or dampen their own emotional responses; thus it meets exclusion E7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli used for ER and EPT tasks), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts/task-evoked activations), I10 (whole-brain analyses reported), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed participants to perform an emotion-labeling task (affect labeling), which constitutes an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6). The emotional stimuli were visual (faces) (I7). The sample is a nonclinical adult sample reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (emotion label > gender label) and an unregulated viewing contrast (observe > fixation) (I9). Group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates are reported (I10) and results are presented in text/tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be included.

Exclusion E4 applies: the study’s primary task activation results are reported using an a priori ROI (bilateral amygdala) rather than a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates. Although a whole-brain PPI (connectivity) analysis is reported, the paper does not present a whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map (contrast of emotion viewing) with peaks in standard space. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: fearful vs. happy). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy—the task was implicit gender discrimination, not reappraisal or other regulation), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported), I11 (no whole-brain activation peaks/tables provided). Because I10/I11 are not satisfied and the paper relies on ROI results without a whole-brain task activation map, it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task-evoked evidence and must be excluded.

This full text meets the review’s criteria for inclusion as an unregulated viewing fMRI study. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (I7: IAPS/static grayscale images) and includes an unregulated viewing contrast (Negative > Neutral) reported in voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analyses (I9, I10). Results are presented in tables and figures with voxelwise thresholds and reported regions (I11). Sample includes a clinical group and controls (I8). The task was an emotional oddball requiring attention to targets amid emotional distractors; no instruction to regulate emotion was given, so the study does not meet I6 (instructed emotion regulation), but I6 is not required because the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts per I9. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, or empathy/perspective-taking tasks) apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion as an unregulated visual-emotion task with whole-brain activation contrasts.

Exclusion reason: E4 applies — the study reports amygdala task activation using small-volume correction (ROI/SVC) and does not report a whole-brain task-evoked group activation map for the emotion contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adult participants), I9 (reports a within-task contrast: sad vs neutral). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — participants performed autobiographical memory recall, not reappraisal/acceptance or other instructed regulation), I7 (stimuli are script-driven autobiographical recall accompanied by music, not visual emotional stimuli such as pictures or film), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map reported; primary activation was tested with SVC). Full text appears complete: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use distraction (MEMORIZE condition) versus passive viewing to regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS and EmoPics), with female BPD patients and control groups reported separately. The analysis includes within-task contrasts (NEGATIVE>NEUTRAL; MEMORIZE vs VIEW) and group×time×task contrasts, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli with patient and control groups and reports within-task contrasts (emotional conflict adaptation) with coordinate results; however it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements. The meta-analysis requires an instructed emotion regulation task (I6), e.g., reappraise vs look; here regulation is implicit/non-instructed (the study explicitly tests spontaneous, non-instructed adaptation), so I6 is not met. Additionally, the paper reports results only within a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and displays findings within those ROIs (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation map reported), thus failing the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps with peak coordinates (I10). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-task contrasts of emotional viewing (e.g., fear > calm, early > late habituation). Thus it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); the task required detection/response suppression but did not instruct subjects to regulate their emotional responses. Therefore it does NOT meet I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy) and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based (event-related) fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (angry>neutral, fearful>neutral, happy>neutral) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates (FDR-corrected). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis objective explicitly accepts studies where participants view emotional stimuli without regulating; the study therefore satisfies the unregulated-viewing criterion (I9). The full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain group-level analysis with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Given these points, the study is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis examining neural responses during viewing (unregulated) of visual emotional stimuli.

The study is EXCLUDED. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; participants were not told to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotion), I7 (stimuli were auditory tones and white-noise UCS, not VISUAL stimuli), I9 (no within-task contrast of instructed emotion regulation or an unregulated visual-viewing contrast as required), I10 (analyses were restricted to anatomical ROIs rather than reporting a whole-brain, voxelwise group map). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (results are reported using ROI-restricted analyses with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not satisfy the review objective of fMRI studies of instructed regulation or viewing of visual emotional stimuli.

Exclusion: E5 applies — the study reports resting-state and seed-based functional connectivity analyses (amygdala connectivity) and does not provide a whole-brain task-evoked activation map relevant to instructed emotion regulation. Inclusion: I8 is satisfied (sample characteristics: female clinical BPD group and healthy controls reported separately). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/distancing was employed), I7 (regulated stimuli are not visual emotional images; stress was induced via the Montreal Imaging Stress Task and incision, not visual emotional stimuli), I9 (no within-task contrast reflecting emotion regulation like “reappraise > look”), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported), and I5 (while an fMRI task was used for stress induction, the study does not constitute a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI study as required by the review objective). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) and reports within-task contrasts comparing negative versus neutral trials (attending and ignoring conditions). It provides group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with MNI coordinates and tables/figures, and the full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (reappraisal) was used, the review objective allows unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > neutral), which this paper reports. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, empathy/perspective-taking-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E5 applies: the study reports only seed-based task connectivity (amygdala seed) results rather than whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Although it contains a task contrast (Violence > Non-Violence) and reports voxelwise connectivity maps with peak coordinates, these are connectivity (seed-to-voxel) analyses and no conventional whole-brain task activation (e.g., emotion > neutral) activation map is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: violent video game clips), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast analogue, PLAC Violence > PLAC Non-Violence), I10 (group-level voxelwise maps with MNI coordinates provided for connectivity results), I11 (results described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (none additionally unmet beyond the connectivity-only issue). Full text appears complete.

This study is EXCLUDED because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Instead, the task required attending to and classifying visual stimuli (face/scene valence), probing implicit emotion regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces and scenes), I8 (sample includes adolescents), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts such as threatening > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster correction), and I11 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E7 not applicable). Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I6) is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis: although it is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study (I5) with an eligible sample (I8) and reports group-level whole-brain results (I10) and acceptable reporting (I11), it does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). The paradigm used math and word verification tasks that incidentally evoke anxiety rather than instructions to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotional responses; stimuli are cognitive problems rather than visual emotional stimuli of the type required (I7 not met). The paper also does not report within-task contrasts specifically labeling instructed emotion regulation (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

The article is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (reinterpretation) to downregulate desire for visually presented food images. It reports within-task contrasts (REGULATE_TASTY > ADMIT_TASTY) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual IAPS pictures, with patient and healthy control groups and within-task contrasts (e.g. negative > neutral), so it meets I5, I7, I8, and I9. However, participants were instructed to anticipate and view stimuli rather than to use an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). Critically, the fMRI analysis was a hypothesis-driven ROI analysis (predefined spherical ROIs) and the paper reports ROI beta-weights rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or peak coordinates; thus it fails I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI results, no whole-brain analysis). Because E4 is met and key inclusion criteria (I6 and I10) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study (I5) of schizophrenia patients and matched controls (I8). It reports within-task emotion contrast (negative vs neutral olfactory stimulation) (I9) and provides group-level whole-brain results with peak coordinates/tables (I10, I11). However, it does NOT meet critical eligibility requirements for this review: the emotional stimuli are olfactory (odorants), not VISUAL, so I7 is not met. Also, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no emotion-regulation instruction such as reappraisal/acceptance/distancing), so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply to this report. Because inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to regulate emotion (explicit 'Regulate' vs 'Look' instructions using cognitive-linguistic reappraisal strategies), used visual stimuli (static photographs of harsh faces and violent scenes), included both a clinical group (SAD) and a demographically-matched healthy control group with results reported separately, and presents within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (e.g. Regulate > Look; Look Harsh Face > Neutral) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates in Talairach space. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (i.e., the full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) with an emotional picture-processing task and explicit contrasts comparing negative, positive, and neutral conditions. Although participants were not instructed to apply an emotion-regulation strategy, the study reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., negative expected pictures vs neutral/positive) at the group level and provides whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses with reported significant clusters and coordinates. The sample includes a patient group (Takotsubo) and matched healthy controls reported separately. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for studies that examine viewing (unregulated) of visual emotional stimuli and provides whole-brain task activation results suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal paradigm (Observe, Maintain, Suppress) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (Maintain>Observe; Suppress>Maintain) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and tables/figures. Both cocaine-dependent and control groups are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing complete assessment. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs participants to regulate emotional responding (upregulate left amygdala during a happy memory induction; I6), includes an eligible sample (MDD patients; I8), reports within-task contrasts (Happy Memories vs Rest/Count; I9), and provides whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses and coordinates (PPI and group maps; I10). However, the regulated emotional stimuli are internally generated autobiographical memories rather than externally presented visual emotional stimuli (no IAPS/images/film/video stimuli), so it does not meet I7 (visual emotional stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (sad and neutral film clips) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Sad > Neutral). Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported with peak coordinates in standard space, and the full article includes methods, results, and discussion. The study therefore meets the review’s scope (studies of viewing visual emotional stimuli without regulation) and satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (fearful and neutral faces) and reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (fearful > neutral) at the group level. Whole-brain group analyses with peak coordinates in standard space are reported. Sample includes a clinical PTSD group and traumatized controls reported separately. Although no instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used (I6 not met), the protocol and reported contrasts satisfy the meta-analysis objective by providing unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli and an instructed effortful regulation paradigm (n-back with emotional distractors), reporting within-task contrasts and MNI coordinates; however all neuroimaging analyses were conducted within an a priori region-of-interest mask (frontolimbic and striatal ROIs) and no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps or analyses are reported. Per the review criteria, studies that report ONLY ROI or small-volume-corrected results with no whole-brain analysis must be excluded (E4). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive control/effortful emotion regulation via task demands), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map reported). Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) using visual stimuli (animated Cyberball; I7) in an adolescent sample (I8). It reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (observed inclusion vs observed exclusion; I9) and presents whole-brain, group-level results with peak coordinates and tables (I10, I11). However, the study did NOT instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation), so it fails inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to be met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual, static disorder-related and neutral scene stimuli presented during a feature-based task (CDTD). The paper reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (disorder-related > neutral) and an exploratory whole-brain analysis with reported activation clusters/tables, and includes both a clinical (SAD) group and healthy controls. No instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used, but the review objective allows inclusion of studies that merely view visual emotional stimuli without regulation. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis criteria for unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is a task-based (rtfMRI) experimental study that instructed participants to volitionally regulate anterior insula activity using an instructed strategy (recalling/imagining negative personal events) and then presented visual emotional stimuli (painful pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulation > baseline), whole-brain group-level activation maps with MNI coordinates and appropriate corrections, and includes full methods, results, and discussion. Sample and analyses meet inclusion requirements. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to employ an emotion regulation strategy. Instead, subjects performed a spatial cueing task and were told that faces were irrelevant (i.e., passive/ignored viewing), so no instructed regulation (reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, etc.) occurred. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — faces), I8 (sample acceptable — older and young adults), I9 (reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing; emotion vs neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported), I11 (results described adequately). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 violations). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded solely due to failure to meet I6 (instructed emotion regulation).

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (guided attentional distraction vs evaluation) with visual, static OCD-relevant and aversive images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (evaluation > distraction; OCD-relevant > neutral/aversive) and group-level, whole-brain analyses (with ROI follow-up), with results presented in figures and supplementary tables. Both patient and matched healthy control groups are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task effects). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so it is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of instructed regulation (visual stimuli) and is included.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (Cyberball) and reports whole-brain group analyses of a within-task contrast (rejection > acceptance), it does not meet the requirement that an emotion-regulation strategy be instructed during the task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task/unregulated viewing contrast: rejection>acceptance), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; the study assesses dispositional mindfulness rather than instructing participants to regulate). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (‘distance’) and ‘immerse’ conditions using visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (distance/aversive > immerse/aversive; immerse/aversive > immerse/neutral) and provides group-level whole-brain analyses with MNI coordinates. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli and an instructed cognitive-control task (EFNBACK) with appropriate within-task contrasts (e.g., emotional-distracter vs. no-distracter) and reported MNI peak coordinates, the reported activation results are restricted to predefined ROIs with ROI-based multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim) and PPI analyses constrained to target ROIs. The paper does not present or report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain coordinates outside ROI-restricted results. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive control of emotional response via ignoring emotional distracters), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), and I11 (coordinates reported for ROI clusters). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked group map reported). Consequently the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample reported with patient and control groups), I9 (within-task contrasts: stress > neutral reported), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses with MNI coordinates), I11 (results and coordinates clearly reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy — participants engaged in script-driven imagery without instructions to reappraise, accept, or otherwise regulate emotion), I7 (stimuli are script-driven auditory imagery, not visual stimuli such as pictures or films). Because the meta-analysis requires instructed emotion-regulation tasks of visual stimuli, failure to meet I6 and I7 warrants exclusion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (explicit suppression) and uses priming for implicit suppression during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and other images). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing suppression runs to baseline (e.g., EXP vs BASEEXP), Dm (subsequent memory) contrasts, group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with tables/clusters and ROI analyses, and peak coordinates. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study that directly examines instructed emotion regulation (reappraise > look) and uninstructed viewing (look negative > look neutral) using visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look; look negative > look neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholding, and presents coordinate-based results. Sample is healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs participants to use a cognitive emotion-regulation strategy (positive reappraisal) during the Picture Viewing Task (I6). The regulated stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The sample (clinical participants; transdiagnostic emotional distress disorders) is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Positive Reappraisal vs Negative Attend) and relates activation to behavior (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps using FSL/FLAME with cluster correction and reported results/tables and supplemental figures (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and it is not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore include for the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI with visual stimuli (peer face photographs) in adolescents, reports within-task contrasts (negative vs. positive feedback) and whole-brain results with peak coordinates. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); the task probed natural responses to social feedback rather than instructed regulation. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy). It meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 but not I6, so it must be excluded per the review criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met), uses visual stimuli (colored squares) (I7 met), includes an eligible sample of healthy adults (I8 met), reports within-task contrasts (CS- > CS+ and CS+ > CS-) that qualify as unregulated viewing contrasts (I9 met), and provides group-level whole-brain task analyses with coordinates (I10 and I11 met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Because the review requires all inclusion criteria be met and this paper lacks instructed emotion regulation, it must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly tests instructed cognitive reappraisal (enhance vs. suppress) using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (enhance–suppress) for the emotion regulation fMRI session, conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction, and reports peak coordinates in MNI space (Tables and figures). Participant sample is a healthy group of males (acceptable per I8). Thus all required inclusion criteria for the review are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not non-empirical, does not report only ROI or connectivity results, and includes within-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Recommendation: INCLUDE in the meta-analysis. If desired, extract the reported whole-brain peak coordinates (Tables 1 & 2) and the (enhance> suppress) contrasts for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) presented as distractors during a delayed working-memory task. The paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative emotional > scrambled) and within-group as well as between-group whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (FWE-corrected), and provides full methods, results and discussion. The sample includes OCD patients and matched healthy controls with within-group effects reported. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraisal) was given, the meta-analysis objective allows inclusion of studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; the study therefore provides an appropriate unregulated emotion contrast for inclusion. Connectivity analyses (DCM) are present but whole-brain task activations are also reported, so exclusion criterion E5 does not apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full-text provides a complete task-based fMRI study in which participants (AUD sample) performed instructed emotion-regulation tasks using visual stimuli (IAPS and alcohol/food images). The paper reports within-task contrasts for regulation (REAPPRAISE-Negative > LOOK-Negative; LATER > NOW) and whole-brain group-level activation maps with peak coordinates and cluster correction, plus tables/figures. All inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. The ER task directly matches the meta-analysis objective (regulated vs. unregulated viewing of visual emotional stimuli).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (detach vs permit), uses visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS), includes within-task contrasts for emotion reactivity and regulation (e.g., permit negative > permit neutral; detach negative > permit negative), reports whole-brain exploratory analyses with results/tables, and uses an eligible sample. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; includes whole-brain task activation maps and within-task effects; not only connectivity or ROI-only). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS photographs) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Negative > Neutral and arousal-specific contrasts) analyzed at the group level with whole-brain random-effects maps and reported peak coordinates. The sample (young and older adults) is acceptable. Although the reported results focus on a spontaneous viewing/run before any instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (so no instructed reappraisal contrast is analyzed here), the meta-analysis objective explicitly includes studies that view stimuli without regulating; therefore the study meets the relevant inclusion path. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I11 (coordinates/results clearly described). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly addresses the review question. It uses an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (LOOK/DECREASE) employing cognitive reappraisal instructions (I6) with visual stimuli from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes a clinical group (IGD) and matched controls reported separately (I8). Results include within-task effects (eg, negative vs neutral, look vs decrease; amygdala ROI and within-group comparisons) and contrasts related to regulation (I9). A group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM was conducted and reported with voxel-level thresholding and pFWE correction (voxel p<0.001, pFWE<0.05), with clusters reported in tables/figures (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain task activation (not E4 or E5), includes within-group task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study (not E7). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (partner facial expressions), reporting unregulated viewing contrasts (partner negative > partner neutral) and group-level whole-brain results with coordinates, it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I6: there was no instruction to regulate emotion (participants were explicitly not instructed to regulate). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is a resting-state, seed-based connectivity fMRI investigation in adolescent marijuana users and does not involve a task or instructed emotion regulation. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (reports ONLY seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes adolescents). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli/task; resting-state), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps reported), I11 (not applicable as whole-brain task results are absent). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal/downregulation (I6) of emotional responses to visual stimuli drawn from the IAPS (I7).
