Participants include clinical (bipolar I) and control groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (decrease vs. observe) and unregulated viewing contrasts (observe negative vs. neutral) (I9). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with thresholding and anatomical labeling are reported (cluster Z>2.0, p=.05 corrected), satisfying whole-brain reporting with standard-space localization (I10), and results are clearly described in text and tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. The provided full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with whole-brain results and an appropriate sample (meets I5, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instructions) and thus fails I6. Crucially, the emotional stimuli are words (drug and neutral words), not visual images/film/clips; the review excludes studies using word/sentence stimuli, so it fails I7. No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not meet I6 and I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral; positive > neutral) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected, MNI coordinates). The sample (children and adults) is eligible. Although no explicit emotion regulation instructions were given (i.e., I6 not satisfied), the meta-analysis objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; the study therefore satisfies the necessary inclusion conditions for unregulated viewing studies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a resting-state fMRI seed-based connectivity study using an acute tryptophan depletion challenge; it does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm or visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criteria: E5 applies (reports ONLY resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample description qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli task), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli and whole-brain group analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/other instructed regulation); the task was an oddball target detection with aversive distractors, so inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6).

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using a visual emotional task (approach–avoidance with happy/angry face images) in human participants (police recruits). The task includes explicit instructions requiring cognitive control over automatic emotional action tendencies (incongruent vs. congruent blocks), and the primary neural contrasts reported (incongruent > congruent) index instructed emotional control. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and also reports psychophysiological-interaction connectivity analyses. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI of instructed emotion regulation/control with visual stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain results.

This study is excluded because it uses resting-state fMRI and multivariate machine learning to classify PTSD subtypes rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli used; resting-state, eyes-closed), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level task activation maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports only ROI-masked group analyses (region-of-interest/full-factorial within an a priori relapse mask) and does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with cue-exposure paradigms), I7 (visual stimuli: alcohol and neutral images), I8 (clinical sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrast alcohol > neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; passive cue-reactivity, not reappraisal or other instructed regulation), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group analysis reported). Full text appears complete. Thus excluded because it fails I6 and I10 and meets exclusion E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly investigates instructed cognitive control over emotional/ social-action tendencies using an approach-avoidance (AA) task. The AA task requires participants to override automatic emotional action tendencies (affect-incongruent vs affect-congruent), which constitutes an instructed emotion-regulation/cognitive-control strategy. Emotional stimuli are visual (faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (incongruent > congruent) and links these to stress responsivity. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed and reported (with peak coordinates and SVC ROI results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli and reports unregulated emotion contrasts, but it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task-evoked activation reporting. Specifically, the paper focuses on ROI-based activation and dynamic causal modeling (effective connectivity) among vmPFC, sgACC, and amygdala, and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates. Therefore it falls under exclusions for ROI-only/effective-connectivity-only reporting.

This is a resting-state fMRI study (ALFF and seed-based rsFC) with no task, no instructed emotion-regulation paradigm, and no within-task contrasts or task-evoked activation maps. It therefore does not meet the review’s core inclusion requirements for a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI study. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the paper reports only resting-state and connectivity/ALFF analyses without any whole-brain task activation maps. Inclusion criterion I8 (sample eligibility) is satisfied (older adult participants), but inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), and I10 (whole-brain task-evoked maps) are NOT met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of masked visual emotional faces in chronic marijuana smokers and controls (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy; subjects performed gender discrimination and passively viewed masked affective stimuli, with no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other instructed regulation (violates I6). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (emotion-regulation instruction).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs participants to exert cognitive control over emotional visual distractors (ignore emotional face distractors) during an N-back working memory task, which qualifies as instructed cognitive control of an emotional response. Stimuli are visual (faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotional processing (fearful>neutral; happy>neutral) and an interaction contrast linking emotional distractors with working-memory load, and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported significant clusters (e.g., left IFG BA45). The sample includes a clinical group (schizophrenia) and healthy controls with results reported separately. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional images and reports whole-brain group-level contrasts (negative > neutral) with coordinates, but the fMRI task did not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (it was an emotion identification/discrimination task). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed regulation), though it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation in older adults that reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. However, the regulated stimuli are personalized worry/suppression sentences (script-driven imagery / word/sentence prompts presented on the screen) rather than visual emotional stimuli (e.g., pictures, faces, film). Inclusion criterion I7 requires visual emotional stimuli and specifically excludes studies using word or sentence stimuli or purely script-driven imagery. Therefore the study fails to meet I7 and must be excluded. Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: worry suppression), I8 (eligible sample: elderly clinical + controls), I9 (reports within-task contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (down-regulation via real-time fMRI neurofeedback) using visual aversive pictures in healthy participants, and it reports within-task contrasts (‘regulate > view’) in connectivity analyses. However, the paper presents only seed-based connectivity (PPI) and effective connectivity (DCM) results and does not report a group-level, whole-brain task activation map (task-evoked activation contrasts with whole-brain coordinates) within this full text (activation results are referenced as reported in a prior paper). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity reported without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported in this article). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study of passive viewing of visual emotional stimuli (movie clips of fearful and neutral faces) with a clear within-task unregulated viewing contrast (negative > neutral). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected results with peak activations reported), and includes separate patient (BPD) and healthy control groups. Stimuli are visual; behavioural and imaging analyses include the relevant contrasts. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (i.e., I6 not met), the study provides an unregulated viewing contrast that satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion (I9). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion; supplemental material is not required. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (emotional faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotional face > fixation; happy/fearful vs. neutral). The sample (youth clinical and healthy controls) is eligible. The paper includes whole-brain (exploratory) group-level analyses (reported in supplemental Table S2) in standard space and provides coordinate-based results. Although the task did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal instruction), the meta-analysis objective explicitly accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; therefore the study meets the review’s eligibility (task-based visual emotional stimuli with within-task contrasts and whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplements referenced).

This study used resting-state seed-based functional connectivity in bipolar patients and did not include any task-based emotion regulation fMRI paradigm or visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a task activation map). Inclusion criterion I8 (sample: clinical participants) is met. However it fails to meet required inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation/viewing contrast), and I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps). Full text appears complete and methods/results are provided, but the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of task-evoked emotion regulation to visual stimuli, so it must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (ER and CR tasks) that explicitly instructed an emotion regulation strategy (reappraise/savoring) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS and smoking images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise vs view; smoking cue vs neutral) entered into group-level repeated-measures random-effects analyses and describes significant group×time whole-brain effects (cluster-corrected) in rACC and ventral striatum, and reports seed-to-voxel rsFC analyses. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, and whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (clusters within standard anatomical space), satisfying the review’s criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to regulate emotion (compassion meditation vs. cognitive reappraisal) while viewing visual images from the IAPS. The fMRI task includes Regulate and Attend conditions, and analyses report Negative–Neutral contrasts and Post–Pre training contrasts. The paper reports both ROI and whole-brain voxel-wise analyses, including a significant whole-brain cluster with MNI coordinates in right AI/OFC, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task activation maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (imagery-based reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (colored squares). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly addressing regulation (Attend vs Regulate CS+), uses group-level whole-brain GLM analyses with reported coordinates, and contains full methods, results, and discussion. Participants are healthy adults and analyses include SCR-behavior correlations. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (static facial expressions) (I7). Participants were explicitly instructed to try to become as happy or sad as possible using the faces (an instructed up-regulation/generation strategy), which meets the requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6) and/or qualifies for up-/down-regulation contrasts. The paper reports within-task contrasts of emotion versus baseline (sadness > baseline; happiness > baseline), satisfying the requirement for a within-task emotion regulation or unregulated viewing contrast (I9). Analyses were performed as group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise SPM2 analyses with cluster reporting and anatomical labeling (whole-brain task-evoked maps) consistent with I10; results are described and clusters reported in the text/tables (I11). The full text includes methods, results and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (dynamic faces) with an unregulated viewing contrast (emotions vs. shapes) reported. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) and provides region coordinates/cluster results. Sample includes clinical and healthy control groups. Although the task does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met), the study meets the meta-analysis’ allowance for unregulated viewing contrasts (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it is eligible for inclusion under the unregulated viewing pathway.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces/houses) and reports task contrasts (AF and IF) with within-group results and clinical/control samples. However, all second-level analyses are restricted to a priori ROIs and results are reported from ROI clusters (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map in standard space is provided). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/small-volume-corrected results with no whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal; task is an implicit attention/interference task rather than instructed regulation) and I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation reported). Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual face stimuli in an appropriate sample (I5, I7, I8, I10 satisfied), it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (I6 not met). The task involves impression formation and social-cognitive evaluation rather than an emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraise, accept, distance). While condition>baseline contrasts were modeled for use in PLS, the study does not report within-task contrasts of emotion regulation nor an explicit unregulated viewing contrast of emotional stimuli (I9 not met). The study therefore falls outside the review scope; it also meets exclusion criterion E7 (social/perspective-taking/impression-formation without instruction to amplify or dampen one’s emotional response). Excluded because E7 applies; inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10; inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs participants to use an attention-to-breath (ATB) mindfulness regulation strategy during presentation of aversive visual stimuli (IAPS). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation and passive viewing ([ATB vs PV], [PV vs ATB], picture vs no-picture), and links brain activation to behavioral regulation success. Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported (cluster/FWE thresholds) alongside ROI analyses and coordinate-based results. Sample is healthy adult participants and analyses include emotion-related contrasts and PPI connectivity but also whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

The full text describes an empirical task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation task (enhance/suppress/maintain) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Within-task contrasts (positive suppress > positive maintain and negative suppress > negative maintain) are reported and used in hierarchical linear modeling to predict changes in anhedonia. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with peak coordinates and cluster correction. The sample includes a clinical MDD group and a control group reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs participants to generate cognitive reappraisals (downregulate anger) — i.e., an emotion regulation strategy — satisfying the review focus on reappraisal. Emotional stimuli included photographs (presented with audio stories), qualifying as visual stimuli. The paper reports within-task contrasts (RGT > fixation; RGT > AUT) and whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with voxelwise FWE correction and reported activation coordinates/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and the study should be included.

This study should be excluded because it is not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study. It uses resting-state fMRI effective connectivity (DCM) and diffusion MRI (DTI) tractography, with no instructed emotion-regulation task, no within-task regulation contrasts, and no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/effective connectivity and structural analyses without any whole-brain task activation). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I9 (reports within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded from the meta-analysis focusing on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face-matching with fear and neutral faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (fear > neutral, fear > neutral+control) at the group level. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion; second-level whole-brain analyses and coordinate labeling are reported (tables/figures and supplementary material). The sample is described and eligible. The meta-analysis objective accepts either instructed regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts; this study supplies unregulated viewing contrasts appropriate for inclusion and does not violate any exclusion criteria (it is empirical, reports whole-brain task-evoked maps, and is not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (cognitive downregulation) during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (film clips). This fMRI study uses a task (threat vs. safe cues) and reports ROI-based analyses of percent signal change during handholding conditions; however it does not meet critical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the report uses an ROI-based approach and extracts parameter estimates from predefined ROIs rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates). Full text appears complete.

While this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (I5, I7) with an eligible sample (BD patients and healthy controls; I8), reporting valence contrasts (Negative > Neutral) and providing group-level coordinates/figures (I9, I10, I11), it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses. The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and photos) and reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing (negative vs neutral) with whole-brain group analyses and peak coordinates. This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (static faces) (I7) in an eligible sample (children/adolescents; clinical high-risk group with healthy controls reported separately) (I8). This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (I5, I7). The sample is eligible (healthy adult participants; I8). The study is a task-based fMRI with visual emotional face distracters and reports within-task emotion contrasts and whole-brain exploratory results (in supplements), but it does NOT instruct participants to use an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing). This task-based fMRI study (faces task) contrasts emotion labeling (an incidental/instructed form of emotion regulation) with emotion matching/gender labeling and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., emotion labeling vs emotion matching) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholded Z-statistic images and peak coordinates. Stimuli are visual (faces). Sample includes adolescents and a control group reported separately. Thus it meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of network connectivity in mTBI patients; it does not involve a task-based emotion regulation paradigm or instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting-state only), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps reported). This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli, whole-brain group-level analyses, and within-task contrasts reported. The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with visual stimuli (I5, I7), includes an appropriate sample (I8), and reports an unregulated within-task contrast (negative > positive) relevant to emotion processing (I9). This is an empathy (intentional perspective-taking) fMRI study with visual face stimuli and whole-brain analyses. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast or a pure unregulated ‘view’ contrast distinct from an empathy instruction). Therefore the study should be excluded.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study of frustration in children that includes whole-brain results, but it does not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) or include an explicit regulation instruction. Therefore it fails the required criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (emotional valence > neutral) as well as whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with MNI coordinates. Sample includes patient and control groups reported separately. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (i.e., I6 ‘instructed regulation’ is not present), the meta-analysis objective accepts studies that involve passive/unregulated viewing; the study therefore satisfies the required within-task unregulated contrast (I9). Excluded because the fMRI task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (instructed regulation criterion I6 not met) and the reported fMRI results are reported using small-volume correction/ROI analyses (amygdala SVC) with no accompanying whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map reported, thus violating exclusion criterion E4. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., faces > baseline), and I11 (coordinates/results reported in text). However it fails I6 (no instructed regulation) and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group map). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (angry and neutral faces) and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (Angry > Neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and MNI peak coordinates. Sample is healthy adult participants. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), so the study addresses the review objective and meets the necessary inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive distraction (0-back vs 2-back) during anticipation of negative vs neutral IAPS pictures, qualifying as an instructed antecedent-focused emotion-regulation strategy (attentional deployment/cognitive control). Stimuli were visual (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts addressing regulation effects (e.g. interaction of valence and cognitive load; negative (0-back>2-back) > neutral (0-back>2-back)) and behavioral correlations, all from group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Sample (healthy adult females) is acceptable. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli in a healthy adult sample and reports group-level whole-brain results with peak coordinates, it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) and therefore fails inclusion criterion I6. The reported within-task contrasts (affect-incongruent > congruent in an approach–avoidance task) index voluntary control of action tendencies rather than an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation; thus it does not meet I9 (within-task contrast specifically related to instructed emotion regulation or an unregulated viewing contrast). The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing (e.g., emotion > shape) with whole-brain group analyses and reported coordinates. This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (movie clips and proposal screens) in an Ultimatum Game. The sample (healthy young adult women) is acceptable. Although the study does not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal), the review objective includes studies that involve unregulated viewing; thus the study meets the review’s criteria for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (video clips; I7) with an eligible sample (I8). This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to label affect (an instructed strategy shown to function as incidental emotion regulation), using visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with appropriate within-task contrasts (SC>NT, SP>NT) and whole-brain, group-level analyses reported (satisfying I5, I9, I10, and I11), it does not meet critical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (fearful faces) with both implicit (passive/gender) and explicit (emotion labeling) conditions, and reports within-task emotion contrasts (e.g., fear > neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. This is a task-based fMRI study that uses visual stimuli (video clips) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results; however, participants passively viewed emotion-eliciting videos (sad, gambling, cocaine) with no instruction to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) and no regulation instruction is described. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I6 (regulated-emotion instruction). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — videos), I8 (eligible sample with groups reported), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts / emotion>baseline and condition contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I6) is not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (increase positive, decrease negative) to visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts (increase > watch; decrease > watch), whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in MNI space with coordinates and appropriate multiple-comparison correction, and includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Sample and stimuli meet the review’s eligibility. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with adolescent participants (I8). It reports unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., SWE>NEU), satisfying I9, and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and cluster correction, satisfying I10 and I11. However, the fMRI task did NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instructions), so it fails I6. Critically, the emotional stimuli are written words (swear/negative/positive/neutral words); the review’s inclusion rule excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli, so it fails I7. Because NOT ALL required inclusion criteria are met (I6 and I7 are not satisfied), the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by this paper.

This is a task-based (Cyberball) fMRI study that uses visual stimuli and reports whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (Exclusion vs Inclusion, Inclusion vs Rest) with stereotactic peak coordinates; sample includes clinical group and controls. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or instructed cognitive control); the task elicits an unregulated emotional response to social exclusion rather than an instructed regulation condition. Per the review’s requirement to satisfy all inclusion criteria, I6 (instruction of an emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. Thus the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study (n=18) that instructs attentional deployment (focus-on-gains vs focus-on-missed-chances) as an emotion-regulation manipulation during presentation of visual outcome stimuli. Behavioral and neural contrasts directly test regulation (GF vs MF; e.g., GF>MF) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Opt>Nopt). Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported with MNI peak coordinates and FWE correction. All required elements are present (task fMRI, instructed regulation strategy, visual stimuli, suitable sample, within-task regulation contrasts, whole-brain reporting). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text review: This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (video clips) of participants' own vs unfamiliar children, with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and coordinate tables reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—video clips), I8 (sample qualifies—clinical mothers), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts: Own Positive>Stranger Positive, Own Negative>Stranger Negative), I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses), I11 (coordinates reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; participants passively viewed clips with no instruction to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate). Exclusion criteria: none met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects). Because the protocol requires all inclusion criteria to be satisfied and this study lacks an instructed emotion-regulation condition (I6), it must be excluded from analyses restricted to instructed regulation paradigms. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and an instructed regulation task (Think/No-Think retrieval suppression) that aims to modulate affect. The methods report within-task contrasts (e.g., No-Think > Think; Intrusion vs Non-Intrusion) and relate neural activity to affective outcomes. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with MNI coordinates and FWE correction. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. Thus all inclusion criteria are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Although the instructed strategy is memory retrieval suppression rather than classical reappraisal, criterion I6 explicitly allows instructed cognitive control of an emotional response, which this task implements. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).
